title: Prepending One Machine Step
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $B$ be a natural-number bound, let $l$ be a program label, let $st$ be a seven-register state, and let $c$ be an abstract configuration. If every register of $st$ is at most $B$ and there is a finite run from the configuration obtained by taking one step of the program from $(l,st)$ to $c$, with every configuration before the endpoint satisfying the program guard and register bound $B$, then there is such a run from $(l,st)$ to $c$.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $st$ is at most $B$
A guarded, register-bounded run from the one-step successor of $(l,st)$ reaches $c$
replaced:
Let $x$ be a bit string, $B$ a natural-number bound, $l$ a program label, $st$ a
seven-register state, and $c$ a configuration. If every register of $st$ is at most $B$
and there is a finite run from the configuration obtained by taking one program step
from $(l,st)$ to $c$, with every configuration before the endpoint satisfying the
program’s precondition and register bound $B$, then there is such a run from $(l,st)$ to
$c$.
